_comment: Catan: Starfarers 2019 fixed board, transcribed from Almanac p.16 (strategic set-up picture) and Rulebook pp.2-3. Pointy-top hex grid, odd-r offset coordinates: [row, col], odd rows shifted half a hex to the RIGHT. Row 0 is the victory-point-track edge, column 0 is the Catanian Colonies edge. Neighbours of an even-row hex (r,c): (r,c-1) (r,c+1) (r-1,c-1) (r-1,c) (r+1,c-1) (r+1,c). Neighbours of an odd-row hex: (r,c-1) (r,c+1) (r-1,c) (r-1,c+1) (r+1,c) (r+1,c+1).

catanianColonies._comment: Fixed. Planet colour per lobe hex, Greek-letter disc set per system. Disc values: alpha 4/8/11, beta 8/10/3-12, gamma 3/6/5, delta 2-11/6/9. Beginner set-up assigns them as listed in 'beginnerDisc'; strategic set-up shuffles the 3 discs within the system.

sectorSlots._comment: 15 vacant tri-lobe slots. Each slot lists its 3 lobe hexes. 'region' is near (before the nebula) or far (beyond it). The nebula band itself has no game effect; it only separates the regions for set-up.

sectors._comment: 16 sector tiles (Almanac p.4). Planetary systems list planets in clockwise order; a tile may be rotated freely when placed, so the engine assigns planets to lobe hexes in clockwise order starting from any lobe. 'icon' is the number-disc back icon on that planet (tri = triangle, br = bracket, hex = hex-circle). stars = back of the tile for the strategic/explorer set-up: 1-star tiles go to near slots, 2-star tiles to far slots. The star values are INFERRED (they match the beginner picture and the disc legend on Almanac p.16); confirm against the physical tiles.

numberDiscs._comment: Unexplored discs by back icon. Each planetary system gets exactly one disc of each icon, so pirate bases (P) and ice planets (I) only ever appear on a hex-icon planet.

intersections._comment: Intersections are hex vertices. In a tri-lobe sector the 3 lobe hexes share one CENTRE vertex and three pairwise edges. Planetary system: the centre vertex is NOT a node (ships cannot cross it); each pairwise edge's OUTER vertex is a colony site, adjacent to the 2 planets of that edge. Outpost: the centre vertex IS a node and is the docking point; the 5 docks are not nodes. Empty sector: the centre vertex is an ordinary node. Spaceport sites: the 2 node-neighbours of a spaceport's vertex (the centre vertex is excluded, so these are the vertices along the two planets' outer edges).
